parsed.title: Browser-Only Ransomware: From LLM Hallucinations to a Practical Attack Technique
parsed.summary: Check Point Research found a DeepSeek-attributed Python Flask sample that paired a fake Discord AI upscaler lure with a browser-native ransomware concept, called In-Browser Ransomware. The attack abuses the File System Access API in Chromium browsers, requiring only a user's permission grant and no native payload, exploit, or root access. The sample was incomplete, but the researchers built a working PoC that encrypted pictures in a selected folder on Android and Windows. Android is the most concerning case because photo libraries are highly sensitive, and Chrome 148 allowed selecting the DCIM root. Defenders should treat browser folder-access prompts as security decisions and keep offline or cloud backups.

parsed.title: From cause to cash: a cross-border look at hacktivist activity
parsed.summary: The Kaspersky report tracks 4BID and related hacktivist groups, which have traditionally targeted Russian and Belarusian organizations but now hit companies in Kazakhstan, the UAE, Syria, and Egypt. Attackers typically gain access by exploiting the ProxyShell vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange and then deploy the fd.aspx web shell. They use custom scripts that abuse legitimate tools such as AnyDesk, Panorama9, and Dev Tunnels, and they deploy post-exploitation frameworks including Sliver, Havoc, Mythic Apollo, and AdaptixC2, plus a new backdoor called BlackSalt. The actors also use BYOVD-based EDR killers and the ClearWater and Blackout Locker ransomware. The report notes the geographic shift and growing financially motivated tooling, and it urges defenders to monitor beyond their own perimeter and track emerging threats.

parsed.title: JADEPUFFER: Agentic ransomware for automated database extortion
parsed.summary: JADEPUFFER is an operator whose ransomware campaign was driven end-to-end by a large language model, which Sysdig TRT assesses as the first documented case of agentic ransomware. The attacker gained initial access to an internet-facing Langflow instance via CVE-2025-3248, harvested credentials and MinIO default credentials, then pivoted to a production server running MySQL and Alibaba Nacos. The agent exploited Nacos authentication weaknesses, inserted a backdoor admin, and encrypted 1,342 configuration items with an ephemeral key that was never stored, making recovery impossible. Its payloads were self-narrating and corrected failed steps within seconds, which Sysdig cites as evidence of autonomy. Defenders should patch Langflow, keep secrets away from web-facing servers, harden Nacos and database admin accounts, and apply egress controls.

parsed.title: The SOC Files: ScreenConnect masked as freeware. An inside look at a large-scale campaign
parsed.summary: Kaspersky's MDR team found threat actors abusing the legitimate ScreenConnect remote access tool to deliver AsyncRAT, uncovering a campaign of spoofed freeware sites. The malicious archives masquerade as software such as OBS Studio, DNS Jumper, DS4Windows, and Process Hacker, and they bundle a signed Microsoft install.exe that sideloads a rogue DLL. The DLL silently installs ScreenConnect as a service, which then runs scripts that disable Defender exclusions and UAC prompts and inject AsyncRAT into RegAsm.exe. The sites, more than 90 domains localized into 10 languages, are promoted through SEO to rank at the top of search results. Defenders are advised to enforce application allowlisting, monitor for new remote administration services and scheduled tasks, and filter traffic to unknown domains.

parsed.title: Phantom Squatting: AI-Hallucinated Domains as a Software Supply Chain Vector
parsed.summary: Unit 42 describes "phantom squatting," where adversaries register domains that LLMs hallucinate for legitimate brands to intercept traffic from AI assistants and autonomous agents. Researchers analyzed 913 brands and 685,339 prompts across two LLMs, finding 13,229 URLs flagged as malicious and about 250,000 unregistered hallucinated domains. In the Montana Empire case, an attacker built a postal-service phishing kit with an AI coding assistant after a domain was flagged 23 days earlier by Unit 42's detection pipeline. Other cases included a malicious Android app delivered through a fake postal site and betting and bank credential-harvesting campaigns. Defenders can map likely hallucinated domains, watch registration streams, and gain lead times of 18 to 51 days, since newly registered domains lack reputation and blocklist history.

parsed.title: ARToken: Inside an EvilTokens affiliate panel targeting Microsoft 365
parsed.summary: ARToken is a phishing-as-a-service management panel that Cisco Talos linked to the EvilTokens platform through shared API contracts, PRT persistence endpoints, and deployment patterns. It abuses Microsoft's OAuth device code flow to capture victim tokens and bypass MFA, targeting Microsoft 365 accounts. Its toolkit includes a seven-layer client-side anti-analysis system, encrypted phishing payloads, and features for persistence via Primary Refresh Tokens, inbox access, rule-based evidence suppression, and SharePoint and OneDrive access. The observed lures were targeted vendor-impersonation invoice emails sent to accounts-payable staff at a U.S. life-sciences company, using a reply-pivot and a look-alike SharePoint tenant. Defenders should note that the platform is a full BEC operations environment, not just a device code kit.

parsed.title: DuneSlide: Two Critical RCE vulnerabilities via Zero-Click Prompt Injection in Cursor IDE
parsed.summary: Cato AI Labs disclosed two critical RCE vulnerabilities in the Cursor IDE, dubbed "DuneSlide," each scored 9.8 CVSS and assigned CVE-2026-50548 and CVE-2026-50549. Both flaws let a prompt injection, delivered through an untrusted source such as an MCP server or web search result, cause the LLM agent to overwrite the cursorsandbox binary and escape the sandbox. The first flaw arises because an LLM-set working_directory parameter is added to the sandbox's write allowlist without validation. The second arises because symlink canonicalization falls back to the unresolved symlink path when it fails, letting attackers write outside the project. The attacks require no user interaction and can lead to full system compromise of the host and connected SaaS workspaces. Cursor fixed both issues in version 3.0.

parsed.title: PolinRider: North Korea-Linked Supply Chain Campaign Expands Across Open Source Ecosystems
parsed.summary: PolinRider is a North Korea-linked supply chain campaign tied to the Contagious Interview / Famous Chollima developer-targeting cluster, now spanning npm, Packagist, Go modules, and Chrome extensions. Socket identified 162 malicious release artifacts across 108 packages and extensions. Threat actors compromise maintainer accounts or modify repositories, then plant obfuscated JavaScript loaders hidden with whitespace padding, fake .woff2 font files, or VS Code task files, and they use force pushes to make changes look older. The loader fetches encrypted second-stage material via blockchain RPC services, decrypts it with XOR keys, and runs it with eval(), with DEV#POPPER and OmniStealer observed so far. Defenders should review GitHub Activity logs, VS Code task configurations, and registry release history, and rebuild affected environments from clean machines and known-good lockfiles.
